A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same guidance-watermarking work. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original watermarking experiments on SD2, Flux, and Sana, alongside detector calibration, false-alarm measurements, robustness tests, and appendix analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds adversarial-attack comparisons, quantitative ablations, and an averaged-watermark-residual analysis.

M1.justification: Section 4 retains the same guidance procedure, cosine loss, transformation-gradient aggregation with PCGrad, clipping, and computational simplifications. The new appendix experiments examine existing components rather than introduce a revised method.

E1.justification: The datasets and generation tasks remain unchanged. Evaluation expands to Gaussian blur, diffusion regeneration, and fixed-key averaging attacks. Rotation and VAE purification already appeared in v1, so their additional results do not constitute wholly new scenario coverage.

E2.justification: The overall baseline roster is retained, but comparator participation expands for VAE purification: v1 Figure 5 compares SSig with G-SSig, whereas v2 Figure 4 additionally compares G-VS with Tree-Rings and Gaussian Shading. The original comparison remains in v2 Figure 7.

E3.justification: Existing benchmark settings remain unchanged. Added attack tests specify 500 images for regeneration/purification, 50 for averaging, regeneration steps of 2–10, and fixed-key averaging with PSNR-matched attack strength. New ablation settings are also documented, although Appendix B.2 and Table 6 inconsistently identify the simplification being removed.

E4.justification: v2 substantially extends analysis beyond v1's qualitative guidance examples and late-step study. It adds quantitative guidance-strength/clipping sweeps, quality measurements for guidance-step choices, a simplification ablation, regeneration and averaging attacks, and an averaged-residual study of content dependence (Appendices B and D.3; Figure 4).

E5.justification: The new reproducibility statement explicitly reports fixed random seeds, without specifying their values or establishing additional repeated runs. The earlier false-alarm uncertainty analysis and distribution plots are retained; no new confidence intervals or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain their numerical results, but several result families are added. Table 2 adds blur and rotation entries; rotation capacities are 0, 27, and 194 bits for Gaussian Shading, G-SSig, and G-VS. Figure 4, Figure 9, Figure 17, and Tables 5–6 add attack, sensitivity, residual, and quality findings rather than demonstrate same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The formal assumptions, guidance and loss equations, spectrum definition, whitening formulation, and Appendix C false-alarm derivations are retained. The new ablations and mechanistic explanations introduce no new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: converting post-hoc detectors into in-generation watermarking through guidance, avoiding retraining, improving robustness, and preserving image semantics and quality. Additional experiments support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 links resistance to averaging attacks to content-dependent residuals and offers a semantic-drift explanation for degraded simplification-ablation results. It also removes v1's conjecture about exploiting Stable Signature's Fourier peaks to remove watermarks. The principal content-dependence and computational-cost limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds an official implementation URL and identifies PyTorch, diffusers, and the Grid'5000 infrastructure. Existing hyperparameters, hardware, throughput, and third-party resource information are retained. Code-access documentation is inconsistent because Appendix F also gives the placeholder 'repository XYZ (provided upon acceptance)'.

R1.justification: v2 adds attack-related citations to Abdelnabi and Fritz, Liu et al., Nie et al., and Pei Yang et al., while removing Bas and Butora alongside the Fourier-attack discussion. The broader related-work organization and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations and front matter, adds reproducibility and acknowledgment sections, subdivides Appendix B, and inserts a methodological-comparison appendix. These are localized structural and explanatory additions; most existing prose and the main section sequence are preserved.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with method/comparison diagrams, adversarial-attack curves, sensitivity plots, residual visualizations, and two new tables. Table 2 gains two attack columns and captions receive clarifications. Existing figures are largely retained and relocated or renumbered.

improvement.justification: The added adversarial tests and quantitative ablations strengthen an already extensive evaluation, while the diagrams and implementation information improve understanding and reproducibility. These benefits outweigh localized documentation problems. However, contradictory gradient/simplification descriptions in Appendix B.2 and Table 6, together with conflicting code-availability wording, limit the reliability and clarity of some additions.
